panels.title: Head lag (slots)
panels.description: Wall-clock slot minus head slot. Healthy steady state oscillates between 0 and 1: head sits 1 behind for the first seconds of each slot, until that slot's block arrives. Sustained >2 is the alert condition.

panels.title: Connected peers
panels.description: Summed across the client label: lean_connected_peers is exported one series per client, so the raw metric must be aggregated.

panels.title: Pending blocks
panels.description: Blocks held waiting on a parent the store does not have. A climbing value means the node is receiving blocks it cannot connect.

panels.title: Running version
panels.description: Build each follower is running, from lean_node_info. Set once at startup, so a change here means the process was restarted on a new build. A node that is down has no row.

panels.title: Head slot vs wall-clock slot
panels.description: These two lines should be indistinguishable at this zoom. Visible daylight between them is the node falling behind.

panels.title: Head lag
panels.description: Red line marks the alert threshold.

panels.title: Distance from head
panels.description: Mainnet finality trails the head by ~2 epochs (64 slots) in normal operation.

panels.title: Fewest peers on any custody column
panels.description: The custodian count of the worst-supplied column this node samples, one line per node: min over lean_custody_column_peers. A block is held until every sampled column arrives, so this is the column that stalls import off the tip. Taken with min_over_time inside each step, so a dip shorter than the step on a long range still shows. Thresholds match "Peers per custody column" in the Peers row, which says which column it is.

panels.title: Head computation time
panels.description: How long one fork-choice head computation takes. The specification's per-root get_weight made this seconds at mainnet scale; the single-pass weight fold made it milliseconds.

panels.title: Head computation share of the chain actor
panels.description: Seconds of head computation per second of wall clock. The chain actor is single-threaded and also imports blocks, so this is the fraction of it that fork choice alone consumes: at 0.47 the follower could not keep up with 12s slots.

panels.title: Fork choice reorgs (1h rate)
panels.description: Shallow reorgs are normal on mainnet; a sustained climb is not.

panels.title: Peers by direction
panels.description: Connected peers by which side opened the connection. Inbound supply on mainnet is unbounded and unchosen; an outbound peer is one this node picked, and is the only kind it can aim at a column it needs. The dashed line at 60 is the outbound reservation: outbound sitting at zero under a full inbound table is the state that stalled the follower for two days.

panels.title: Peers per custody column
panels.description: Connected peers known to custody each column this node samples. A block is held until every sampled column arrives, so a column at zero is a stall waiting to happen and is invisible in a total peer count. A peer counts only once it has answered metadata/3 or arrived with a usable cgc, so this is a floor on real supply.

panels.title: Peer bookkeeping vs swarm connection counters
panels.description: Connections the libp2p swarm still charges against the limits, minus the peers this node believes it holds. The limits are enforced against the swarm's count, so a gap that grows and never returns is a connection consuming a slot no live peer is using. A small steady gap is expected: this counts connections and the other counts peers, and a peer may hold up to two (QUIC and TCP).

panels.title: Goodbye reasons: why peers say they drop us
panels.description: goodbye/1 messages received per minute, by the reason code the peer sent (lean_peer_goodbye_total). The only disconnect signal that is not an inference. too_many_peers (blue) means the peer had no room; bad_score (orange), banned and banned_ip (red) mean it decided against this node. The two call for opposite responses and look identical from the socket. Codes above 127 follow lighthouse's GoodbyeReason; other is the residue.

panels.title: Disconnect causes, as libp2p reports them
panels.description: Peers fully disconnecting per minute, by the cause libp2p reported for the last connection's close (lean_peer_disconnect_cause_total). Charged on the same event as lean_peer_disconnection_events_total, so the two total alike; this splits its uninformative error bucket. quic_application_close is the peer's application closing (libp2p's normal close after a goodbye, or go-libp2p's connection gater); yamux_closed and clean_close are deliberate TCP closes; unexpected_eof and connection_reset are sockets dropped under us. io_other is the residue and should stay near zero.

panels.title: Goodbye reasons, share of all goodbyes
panels.description: Of the goodbyes received, the share that said the peer had no room (too_many_peers) and the share that said it decided against this node (bad_score, banned, banned_ip). The first is the mainnet inbound cap and is nothing this node can fix; a rising second share is this node being scored down or banned. Whatever the two leave is the other reasons. A 30m window, since rejections arrive at around one a minute and a 5m ratio of them is mostly noise.

panels.title: Disconnects the peer explained with a goodbye
panels.description: Goodbyes received per peer fully disconnecting: roughly the share of disconnects where the peer said why. The rest are the silent closes the cause panel above tries to read. Approximate, since the two are counted on separate events: a goodbye lands just before the disconnect it causes, so the ratio can briefly pass 1. 30m window.

panels.title: Disconnections by specified reason
panels.description: Peers fully disconnecting per minute, by the leanMetrics-specified reason (lean_peer_disconnection_events_total). Only this counter is on every node, so it is the one to compare followers by. error means only that libp2p handed back a cause; the two panels above say which.

panels.title: Cause counter against the specified counter
panels.description: Both counters are charged on the same event, a peer's last connection closing, so each dashed line should sit on the solid one of its direction. A gap means a close reached one counter and not the other. Only nodes that export the cause counter are shown.

targets.expr: sum by (node, direction) (rate(lean_peer_disconnection_events_total{node=~"$node"}[5m])) * 60 and on (node) sum by (node) (lean_peer_disconnect_cause_total{node=~"$node"})

panels.title: Import, end to end (arrival → attestable), per block
panels.description: One block from the wire to **attestable**: the head that includes it is computed and its payload is validated, so a validator can attest to it. Spans every hold and, since the import no longer waits for the execution client (#773), the wait for its VALID answer too. Per block, from the node's own ClickHouse rows (block_events, `--telemetry.clickhouse-url`); pick the node with the `ClickHouse node` variable. Only blocks that became attestable are shown.

panels.title: Import, end to end (arrival → attestable), over time
panels.description: One block from the wire to **attestable**: the head that includes it is computed and its payload is validated, so a validator can attest to it. Spans every hold and, since the import no longer waits for the execution client (#773), the wait for its VALID answer too. Per block, from the node's own ClickHouse rows (block_events, `--telemetry.clickhouse-url`); pick the node with the `ClickHouse node` variable. Only blocks that became attestable are shown. Percentiles over the blocks in each interval.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  $__timeInterval(received) AS time,
  quantile(0.99)(total_ms) AS p99,
  quantile(0.9)(total_ms) AS p90,
  quantile(0.5)(total_ms) AS p50,
  avg(total_ms) AS mean
FROM (
  SELECT
      block_root,
      minIfOrNull(event_date_time, stage IN ('received', 'import_start')) AS received,
      (toUnixTimestamp64Nano(minIfOrNull(event_date_time, stage IN ('attestable', 'fc_head_end'))) - toUnixTimestamp64Nano(minIfOrNull(event_date_time, stage IN ('received', 'import_start')))) / 1e6 AS total_ms
  FROM block_events
  WHERE event_date_time BETWEEN $__fromTime - INTERVAL 1 MINUTE AND $__toTime + INTERVAL 1 MINUTE
    AND meta_client_name = '${client}'
    AND column_index IS NULL
  GROUP BY block_root
)
WHERE received BETWEEN $__fromTime AND $__toTime AND total_ms IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY time
ORDER BY time

panels.title: Import cost, waits excluded, per block: start of the epoch
panels.description: Only each epoch's first block: the one whose state transition runs the epoch processing, which is slot 0's block, or the next block when slot 0 has none. Where a block's import work goes. Each band is one section's time for that block, stacked, so the top of the stack is the block's import work. Compare it against Import, end to end: the gap is time spent waiting. Excluded from the stack: the mailbox queue, the holds (defer, parent_wait, cascade_wait, columns_wait), the writer hand-off (writer_wait), the per-arrival sections (get_head, fcu) and every wait for the EL's verdict (`engine`, whether inline or after the import). Per block, from the node's own ClickHouse rows (block_events, `--telemetry.clickhouse-url`); pick the node with the `ClickHouse node` variable. Only blocks that became attestable are shown.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  slot,
  coalesce((toUnixTimestamp64Nano(decode_end) - toUnixTimestamp64Nano(received)) / 1e6, 0) AS "decode",
  coalesce((toUnixTimestamp64Nano(admit_end) - toUnixTimestamp64Nano(admit_start)) / 1e6, 0) AS "admit",
  coalesce((toUnixTimestamp64Nano(guards_end) - toUnixTimestamp64Nano(guards_start)) / 1e6, 0) AS "guards",
  coalesce((toUnixTimestamp64Nano(coalesce(da_available, da_check_end)) - toUnixTimestamp64Nano(da_check_start)) / 1e6, 0) AS "da_check",
  coalesce(greatest(0, (toUnixTimestamp64Nano(stf_done) - toUnixTimestamp64Nano(stf_start)) / 1e6 - coalesce((toUnixTimestamp64Nano(writer_wait_end) - toUnixTimestamp64Nano(writer_wait_start)) / 1e6, 0)) + coalesce((toUnixTimestamp64Nano(stf_spec_end) - toUnixTimestamp64Nano(stf_spec_start)) / 1e6, 0), 0) AS "stf",
  coalesce((toUnixTimestamp64Nano(block_atts_end) - toUnixTimestamp64Nano(block_atts_start)) / 1e6, 0) AS "block_atts"
FROM (
  SELECT *, slot = min(slot) OVER (PARTITION BY intDiv(slot, 32)) AS epoch_first
  FROM (
  SELECT
      block_root,
      maxOrNull(slot) AS slot,
      minIfOrNull(event_date_time, stage IN ('received', 'import_start')) AS received,
      minIfOrNull(event_date_time, stage = 'decode_end') AS decode_end,
      minIfOrNull(event_date_time, stage = 'queue_end') AS queue_end,
      minIfOrNull(event_date_time, stage = 'defer_start') AS defer_start,

  coalesce(greatest(0, (toUnixTimestamp64Nano(least(fcu_end, attestable)) - toUnixTimestamp64Nano(fcu_start)) / 1e6), 0) AS "fcu",
  coalesce(if(stf_spec_end IS NULL, NULL, greatest(0, (toUnixTimestamp64Nano(el_verdict) - toUnixTimestamp64Nano(stf_spec_end)) / 1e6)), 0) + greatest(0, (toUnixTimestamp64Nano(attestable) - toUnixTimestamp64Nano(greatest(block_atts_end, coalesce(fcu_end, block_atts_end)))) / 1e6) AS "engine",

toUnixTimestamp64Nano(coalesce(decode_end, received))) / 1e6, 0) + coalesce((toUnixTimestamp64Nano(defer_end) - toUnixTimestamp64Nano(defer_start)) / 1e6, 0) + coalesce((toUnixTimestamp64Nano(admit_end) - toUnixTimestamp64Nano(admit_start)) / 1e6, 0) + coalesce((toUnixTimestamp64Nano(guards_end) - toUnixTimestamp64Nano(guards_start)) / 1e6, 0) + coalesce((toUnixTimestamp64Nano(parent_wait_end) - toUnixTimestamp64Nano(parent_wait_start)) / 1e6, 0) + coalesce((toUnixTimestamp64Nano(if(columns_wait_start > cascade_wait_start AND columns_wait_start < cascade_wait_end, columns_wait_start, cascade_wait_end)) - toUnixTimestamp64Nano(cascade_wait_start)) / 1e6, 0) + coalesce((toUnixTimestamp64Nano(coalesce(da_available, da_check_end)) - toUnixTimestamp64Nano(da_check_start)) / 1e6, 0) + coalesce((toUnixTimestamp64Nano(columns_wait_end) - toUnixTimestamp64Nano(columns_wait_start)) / 1e6, 0) + coalesce(greatest(0, (toUnixTimestamp64Nano(stf_done) - toUnixTimestamp64Nano(stf_start)) / 1e6 - coalesce((toUnixTimestamp64Nano(writer_wait_end) - toUnixTimestamp64Nano(writer_wait_start)) / 1e6, 0)) + coalesce((toUnixTimestamp64Nano(stf_spec_end) - toUnixTimestamp64Nano(stf_spec_start)) / 1e6, 0), 0) + coalesce((toUnixTimestamp64Nano(writer_wait_end) - toUnixTimestamp64Nano(writer_wait_start)) / 1e6, 0) + coalesce((toUnixTimestamp64Nano(block_atts_end) - toUnixTimestamp64Nano(block_atts_start)) / 1e6, 0) + coalesce(greatest(0, (toUnixTimestamp64Nano(least(get_head_end, attestable)) - toUnixTimestamp64Nano(get_head_start)) / 1e6), 0) + coalesce(greatest(0, (toUnixTimestamp64Nano(least(fcu_end, attestable)) - toUnixTimestamp64Nano(fcu_start)) / 1e6), 0)) - (coalesce(if(stf_spec_end IS NULL, NULL, greatest(0, (toUnixTimestamp64Nano(el_verdict) - panels.title: Blocks: $client
panels.description: Blocks first received in the time range that became attestable. Per-block timings the node wrote to ClickHouse (`--telemetry.clickhouse-url`, Silver's `block_events` layout, ClickHouse on eth-4). Steps, in order, adding up to arrival -> attestable: **before the STF** (decode, actor queue, admission and checks), **wait for columns** (held until its custody columns arrived), **STF + EL** (`engine_newPayload` and the speculative state transition run side by side, then the import that uses the verdict), **head** (block attestations, then the head recomputation that makes the block attestable). Failed blocks and blocks still held have no row. Pick the node with the `ClickHouse node` variable.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT count() FROM (
  SELECT
    received, slot, source, verdict, block_root, arrival_ms, attestable_ms,
    (toUnixTimestamp64Nano(exec_start) - toUnixTimestamp64Nano(received)) / 1e6 - columns_wait_ms AS before_ms,
    columns_wait_ms,
    (toUnixTimestamp64Nano(stf_done) - toUnixTimestamp64Nano(exec_start)) / 1e6 AS exec_ms,
    (toUnixTimestamp64Nano(attestable) - toUnixTimestamp64Nano(stf_done)) / 1e6 AS head_ms,
    (toUnixTimestamp64Nano(attestable) - toUnixTimestamp64Nano(received)) / 1e6 AS total_ms,
    (toUnixTimestamp64Nano(el_verdict_at) - toUnixTimestamp64Nano(el_sent)) / 1e6 AS el_ms,
    (toUnixTimestamp64Nano(stf_spec_end) - toUnixTimestamp64Nano(stf_spec_start)) / 1e6 AS stf_spec_ms,
    (toUnixTimestamp64Nano(stf_done) - toUnixTimestamp64Nano(stf_start)) / 1e6 AS stf_ms,
    (toUnixTimestamp64Nano(get_head_end) - toUnixTimestamp64Nano(get_head_start)) / 1e6 AS get_head_ms
  FROM (
    SELECT
      block_root,
      maxOrNull(slot) AS slot,
      anyIf(source, stage IN ('received', 'import_start')) AS source,
      minIfOrNull(event_date_time, stage IN ('received', 'import_start')) AS received,
      minIfOrNull(time_into_slot_ms, stage IN ('received', 'import_start')) AS arrival_ms,
      minIfOrNull(event_date_time, stage IN ('el_sent', 'el_start')) AS el_sent,
      minIfOrNull(event_date_time, stage IN ('el_verdict', 'el_end')) AS el_verdict_at,
      argMinIf(verdict, event_date_time, stage IN ('el_verdict', 'el_end')) AS verdict,
      minIfOrNull(event_date_time, stage IN ('stf_spec_start', 'cl_start')) AS stf_spec_start,
